body: I only noticed now, but this signal should probably be connected after the loop below. Otherwise this method is called multiple times for each child, because they will be entering tree after this call.

I'm not sure what you mean? The loop just calls this method recursively and this method does not add children to the tree.
And when this signal is emitted for a node, then it is called on the new child node.

When a node branch is added to tree, e.g.
```
Node
  |_Node2
```
Node enters tree, `_connect_to_scene_recursive()` is called for Node, which then calls that method for the child (in the loop).
Then Node2 enters tree, so `_connect_to_scene_recursive()` is called again for Node2, because the signal from parent was connected.

You can test it easily by printing `p_current` at the top of this method. There are many duplicate calls (which are also doubled, because of Shader editor).

It is being called twice, but moving the connect after the loop won't help since the function completely exits by the time the next `child_entered_tree` is emitted.
But now that it is no longer deferred, we may be able to rely on that to recursively connect instead of using a loop at all, I'll look into that.

- For shader editor, I am planning to address it after https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/121699, since I want to move where it is structurally to just the singleton.

> moving the connect after the loop won't help since the function completely exits by the time the next child_entered_tree is emitted.

Right, I guess the connection would need to be deferred, which is questionable.

> we may be able to rely on that to recursively connect instead of using a loop at all

That could work too.
